prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (alias Juniper), 24/7 regional EMS dispatch: intake, triage, ambulance dispatch under clinical/jurisdictional protocols. Jurisdictions own resources/policy. Zones have primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center. Intake creates incident record. Center preserves original caller report (confirmed vs estimate), escalates readiness gaps, produces Unit Staging Change Card, records authorization time and unit-selection reason, and maintains regional coverage picture from unit locations, crew reports and readiness. Actors: - Call Taker Mara (alias Larkspur): location first, then patient, hazards, access; produces Caller Location Correction Slip. - Triage Supervisor (alias Copperfield): assigns and justifies priority; escalates to Medical Director; sends Pediatric Acuity Note. - Regional Medical Director: clinical policy. - Dispatcher: recommends unit after priority confirmed; authorization per regional rules; states gate constraints and uncertainty; corrects discrepancies by fresh transmission. - Shift Commander (alias Sundial): approves exceptions and staging moves after reviewing coverage picture; shall not override Medical Director or crew. - Radio Coordinator (alias Mistral): selects and confirms talkgroup; transmits incident ID, location, priority, assignment, hazards over Regional Radio Network; retries and alerts dispatch supervisor if no acknowledgment; confirms route changes before diversion; sends Coverage Gap Bulletin when coverage falls below threshold. - Paramedic Crew: acknowledges and repeats location and priority; handoff when acknowledged and details confirmed; reports route conflicts; reports status (available, responding, on scene, transporting, unavailable) promptly; stays at staging point until reassigned. - Hospital Liaison Desk (alias Kestrel): destinations; coordinates with Emergency Department; produces Bedside Arrival Receipt. - Emergency Department; Riverside Trauma Center. - Fleet Maintenance Cell (alias Bluejay): restricted vehicles; verifies clearance before available status; produces Battery Swap Voucher. - Data Quality Officer (alias Pebble): flags defects; sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo. Systems: Computer Aided Dispatch Console shows details, priority, travel, staging options. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position/status, matches units. Regional Radio Network carries instructions and acknowledgments. Ambulance Unit 417 follows instructions; reports position/status entering/leaving staging. North Gate Status Board (North Approach Queue Snapshot) and South Gate Status Board (southern access conditions) support routing.

New part:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
